reviewMethod.methodNotesMd: Reviewed the resource-review context, the full `InsurancePlan` StructureDefinition report, the deterministic aggregate as prior context, the local R4/R6 `InsurancePlan` definitions, and the R6 `InsuranceProduct` definition to verify where removed product content moved. The behavior reports were searched for findings whose `affectedResources` include `InsurancePlan`; none were direct. Shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings were treated as context only.

r4Maturity.effectMd: R4 `InsurancePlan` was FMM 0 trial-use, so the standards burden to preserve every R4 wire shape is weak. That lowers the presumption against remodeling, but it does not erase the practical business risk in payer/product status, identifiers, coverage, network, contact, and plan cost data.

overall.oneLineConclusion: R6 keeps `InsurancePlan` but remodels it from a combined product/plan container into plan resources linked to `InsuranceProduct`; nontrivial R4 data needs a split, while identifier/type/status compatibility still has review value.

reasoning.thesisMd: The actual migration shape is a same-name resource remodel, not a simple element cleanup. R4 `InsurancePlan` carried product-level identity, status, ownership, contacts, endpoints, coverage benefits, and repeatable nested plan offerings. R6 moves product facts to `InsuranceProduct`, leaves `InsurancePlan` as the individual plan offering, adds `InsurancePlan.product`, and hoists former `plan[]` children to the root. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable for realistic R4 use, but not so absolute that each additional compatibility break becomes irrelevant.
reasoning.migrationShapeMd: The core transform is to create or match an `InsuranceProduct` for the R4 product-side content, then create one R6 `InsurancePlan` for each R4 `InsurancePlan.plan` repetition, preserving cost, network, and coverage-area facts at the new root. The same-name resource identity and all-optional base elements mean sparse R4 instances may not require a full split, so `Partial` is more precise than an unconditional `Yes`. For normal product-directory data, however, path-preserving migration is unsafe: `identifier` and `type` retain familiar paths but now identify/classify the plan rather than the product.
reasoning.compatibilityLeverageMd: The resource redesign is broad enough that migration planning dominates for product fields and the removed `plan[]` backbone once the split is accepted. Still, the best standards posture is not `migration-program-dominates`: low-cost preservation or explicit conversion rules for stable-looking paths can prevent silent business errors. `InsurancePlan.identifier`, `InsurancePlan.type`, and moved modifier `status` are the areas where compatibility preservation remains high leverage despite the broader remodel.
reasoning.lessBreakingAlternativesMd: Retaining all old product fields and the old repeatable `plan[]` backbone as deprecated content would preserve more R4 instances, but it would also leave duplicate product and plan representations with conflict/precedence rules, so those breaks are mostly local migration chores after accepting the new normalized model. The more avoidable concerns are narrower: avoid reusing `InsurancePlan.type` with a different meaning and lower max, make `identifier` migration source-path-aware, and provide explicit transitional handling for the moved modifier `status`.
reasoning.behaviorImpactMd: No direct operation, search, or HTTP behavior finding was scoped to `InsurancePlan`. The shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior findings are relevant to the general R6 ecosystem but do not change this resource-level conclusion. Separate search-parameter migration may still be needed because product and plan facts moved across resources, but that is not represented as a direct behavior finding in the supplied reports.
reasoning.comparisonToDeterministicAggregateMd: The deterministic aggregate concluded `Partial` and `preserve-where-low-cost-but-expect-resource-migration`; I agree with those two conclusions. I characterize the migration shape as `major-model-remodel` rather than merely moderate because the resource's business object changed from combined product plus nested plans to plan resources backed by `InsuranceProduct`. The low R4 FMM prevents treating the whole redesign as presumptively unacceptable.
reasoning.uncertaintyMd: Confidence is high for the structural shape because the R4/R6 StructureDefinitions and R6 `InsuranceProduct` are available locally. Uncertainty remains around official rationale, official conversion maps, terminology expansions, real-world prevalence for this FMM 0 resource, and whether the ballot4 R6 content will change before final publication.

findingConsiderations.title: InsurancePlan was split from a combined product/plan resource into a plan resource backed by InsuranceProduct
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the organizing change: the resource name survives, but the business object shifts. It makes a same-resource copy unsafe and requires product matching/creation plus plan-resource creation for nontrivial R4 instances.

findingConsiderations.title: Product metadata, contacts, endpoints, ownership, and coverage benefits were removed from InsurancePlan
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: These removals are not isolated churn; they are the concrete product half of the split. Once the R6 model is accepted, migration must move these facts to `InsuranceProduct`, but official maps or transitional fields would materially reduce implementation risk.

findingConsiderations.title: Repeatable R4 InsurancePlan.plan backbone was removed and its child plan data was hoisted to the R6 InsurancePlan root
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the plan half of the split. R4 instances with multiple `plan` repetitions generally need to become multiple R6 `InsurancePlan` resources, so migration requires identity/reference policy rather than a local rename.

findingConsiderations.title: Modifier element InsurancePlan.status was removed from InsurancePlan and moved to InsuranceProduct.status
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: `status` follows the product move, but it was a modifier and carries active/draft/retired semantics. Dropping or misplacing it can make inactive products look usable, so conversion guidance or a transitional alias has higher value than an ordinary moved optional field.

findingConsiderations.title: InsurancePlan.type changed from repeatable product type to single plan classification
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is the most avoidable-looking local break: it both narrows cardinality and reuses a stable path with a different business meaning. A renamed R6 plan-classification element, a legacy alias, or stronger normative conversion rules would reduce silent mapper errors.

findingConsiderations.title: InsurancePlan.identifier kept the path but changed from product identifier to plan/group identifier semantics
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This is not a base validation break, but it is high-risk because path-based transforms can produce syntactically valid R6 plans carrying product identifiers. That can corrupt matching, search, and deduplication, so explicit source-path-aware mapping guidance remains valuable even after accepting the remodel.

findingConsiderations.title: InsurancePlan-specific invariant requiring identifier or name was removed from InsurancePlan
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: Removing the invariant does not reject old R4 instances in R6. It matters mainly for R6-to-R4 round-tripping and data quality, so it does not drive the R4-to-R6 resource-level migration conclusion.

findingConsiderations.title: R6 added InsurancePlan.product Reference(InsuranceProduct), creating a new cross-resource dependency not representable in R4
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: The optional product reference is additive for R4-to-R6 validation, but it confirms the new cross-resource dependency and is central to down-conversion and product dereferencing policy.

findingConsiderations.title: Core special/profile search parameters changed type metadata for _content, _text, _query, and _profile
findingConsiderations.reasonMd: This shared `Resource`/`DomainResource` behavior context may affect generic clients, but it is not scoped specifically to `InsurancePlan` and therefore was not used to score the resource-level migration burden.

recommendedNextActions.actionMd: Publish or verify official R4-to-R6 conversion maps for the product/plan split, including product resource creation or matching, one-R6-plan-per-R4-`plan` rules, reference/identifier preservation, and round-trip policy.

Revisit the `InsurancePlan.type` and `InsurancePlan.identifier` changes as standards-review items because they preserve familiar paths while changing business meaning; prefer legacy aliases, distinct R6 naming, or normative conversion warnings over silent path-based migration.
Provide explicit transitional handling for moved modifier `status`, especially for retired/draft/unknown product states, so migrated directories do not treat unavailable products as active.

Review `InsuranceProduct` and InsurancePlan/InsuranceProduct search parameters together with this resource, because product facts and search/indexing responsibilities moved across resource boundaries.

caveats: No official R4-to-R6 diff rationale or executable conversion map was supplied.
The R6 input package is a ballot4 build, so final R6 content may differ.
R4 FMM 0 makes implementation prevalence uncertain; business-risk judgments are based on the semantics of payer directory and coverage data.
Shared `Resource` and `DomainResource` behavior findings were reviewed as context only and did not count as direct `InsurancePlan` behavior breaks.
